speaker: john_shakespeare
text: The thumb knows the seam. I do not need a measure for a pair this fine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I came in to stand, not to count the board.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Gilbert's been counting. He was always a counting child.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: His ticket is in my sleeve. I have not brought it to the bench.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Keep it in the sleeve. The other baker, thirty shillings, and he smiles when he names it. The shoemaker, under two pounds. The skins, a few shillings to a whittawer, and a glover may owe a glover without a speech.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Thou namest them as if the naming made them smaller.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: They are smaller in my own shop. A man may be cheerful inside his own debt.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not answer thee with a sum. The gloves are the work on the board.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Good. A sum is a cold way to speak to a father. Pass the alum. I know which finger of thine is ink.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: His is ink. Thine were alum. I said the finger on Sunday, and I am not saying the church over again.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we are on gloves.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: For a man who pays. That is a cheerful description, and it is not a name.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Do not make him guess a name. I will not have this house put in a book before supper.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not writing the shop. I am looking at a pair cut by eye.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: The eye is still good. The debt is old. The pair is this week's.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Old is not the same word as small. I heard the cheerful size. I am leaving it.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Since thou wilt not open anything, I will. A man may show a thing once.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: They'd have made me a gentleman once, Will. Then wool fell.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The mouse has had the corner. I did not ask thee for it.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Drawn when I was bailiff. A joke, so my fingers have somewhere to be. A Queen's player. Has he friends among the heralds.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A player is a gentleman three hours every afternoon.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: A player! Well. I've seen aldermen do it for nothing and worse.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: I remember the colour of the ink. I will not name the colour. The lamp is for seeing the pair of you off this scrap.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have no friend to send this to. I am not sending it.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: I did not ask thee to send it. Thou hast given me an afternoon. Seen once is enough.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Put it back, John. The wish has been seen. I will not have it asked at supper, and I will not have it filed.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Behind the panel. The mouse may have the rest of the year.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nothing filed. Nothing asked. Nothing promised. I am saying it so I hear myself not saying the other thing.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Supper is pottage. A pattern of arms does not change pottage.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Hear her. The gloves are still the work. Wool fell. That is the sentence I trust.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The sleeve stays a sleeve. I am going in to the pottage.
